04 — TfR1 (conditional binder) · the complete history

This document tells the whole story of the TfR1 conditional-binder campaign, from the captured challenge page to the submitted twenty designs. It names every tool, every decision, and the reason for each. The companion records are lineage.json (the site's own history), notes/ (the research), campaigns/*/ (one plan and one results page per campaign) and records/ (the raw data).

Status: complete 2026-10-30, twenty designs, window closed 2026-11-01. No wet-lab verdict exists; everything below is computational evidence, and the few affinity figures that appear belong to other molecules.

Working-tree note: submission/methodology.md has been edited down in the working copy — the committed version carried a header, per-claim file citations, a final-twenty table and a challenge-3 coherence section that the current file lacks — and experiments/c1-epitope-screen.yaml (campaign 1's screen as a reproducible spec) is deleted but not committed. Nothing here depends on either; numbers come from records/, campaigns/*/results.md and lineage.json.

1. The target and what the three objectives ask for

The assay presents the human transferrin receptor 1 ectodomain (TfR1, also CD71; UniProt P02786-1, residues 121-760, 640 amino acids) as a disulfide-linked homodimer. The design is immobilised, the receptor is in solution, and three conditions are measured: human at pH 7.4, human at pH 6.0, and mouse at pH 7.4 (notes/brief.md, captured 2026-10-23).

Three objectives, in the organizers' order:

  1. pH-selective binding — a measurable KD against human TfR1 at pH 7.4 and no detectable binding at pH 6.0. Designs that bind at both pH values rank after these, by the ratio of their KD at 6.0 to their KD at 7.4.
  2. Mouse cross-reactivity — ranked by how close the mouse-to-human KD ratio is to 1, among designs with a human KD below 1 µM.
  3. Affinity — the lowest human KD at pH 7.4, at a named functional epitope with the evidence linked.

A design counts as binding when its sensorgram gives a fittable curve and a KD, or — where it cannot be fitted — when the association shift clears 300% over the negative control.

The organizers recommend an epitope: the apical domain, the tip of each subunit that arenaviruses, parvovirus B19 and brain-shuttle antibodies bind, which leaves the transferrin site free. They name Tyr211 as the landmark. The two ectodomains, human and mouse, are 78% identical overall but the recommended patch differs at six of nine positions — so objectives 2 and 3 pull against each other from the first decision onward. Chapter 4 is the measurement that settled it.

2. The biology in plain words

What the receptor does. Cells need iron, and iron does not travel loose in blood — a protein called transferrin carries it. TfR1 sits on the cell surface, grabs iron-loaded transferrin and pulls it inside in a bubble of membrane; the cell acidifies that bubble, the acid makes transferrin release its iron, and the receptor carries the empty transferrin back out. It is a pump that runs on a pH change, abundant on dividing cells and at the blood-brain barrier — which is why it is a favourite delivery handle in medicine. Each subunit has three domains, and the apical domain is the tip, away from the transferrin site: viruses and engineered antibodies use it, so a binder there does not compete with the receptor's day job.

What a pH switch is, and why anyone wants one. A binder that holds at pH 7.4 (blood) and releases at pH 6.0 (the acidified bubble) is a shuttle: it grabs its cargo outside the cell, rides in, and lets go where the cell is acidic. The chemistry that buys it is one amino acid. Histidine's side chain is near-neutral at pH 7.4 and largely positive near pH 6.0 — the only common residue whose charge flips inside the assay's own window.

The direction rule, which decides everything about the switch. The challenge wants binding to weaken as the pH falls. So a binder histidine facing a positively charged target residue is neutral at 7.4 and positive at 6.0, and the new like-charge repulsion weakens binding — the asked direction. A binder histidine facing a negatively charged residue gains an attraction instead, which strengthens binding and inverts the objective. The earlier TNF-α challenge in this repo measured exactly that inversion on its own designs: every complex read tighter at pH 6.0, the wrong way (notes/epitope-analysis.md, finding 3). So the anchors here had to be conserved, exposed, positively charged target residues, and the conserved glutamates nearby had to be avoided.

The physical ceiling, stated before any design. One titratable site changes affinity by at most tenfold per pH unit and the assay window is 1.4 pH units, so one histidine buys about 25-fold in theory and much less in practice; a large swing needs two or three coupled sites (campaigns/c3-switch-layer/README.md). The methodology therefore states a direction and a site count and never claims "no detectable binding at pH 6.0", which is a wet-lab observation. And the mouse objective matters because a binder that works in mice can be tested in mice — while being the objective most easily lost by accident, since the recommended epitope is the least conserved surface in the area.

3. The reference structures and what was measured on them

An experimental structure is solved by X-ray diffraction from a crystal of billions of aligned copies — a frozen snapshot of real atoms; a predicted structure (AlphaFold) is a computed guess. This campaign used one of each, and the asymmetry is recorded wherever they meet.

file what it is
inputs/11QC.cif human TfR1 ectodomain homodimer, chains A and B, 639 residues each (author 122-760), three N-linked NAG sugars per chain. The design target.
inputs/11RN.cif the apical complex named in the brief — TfR1 with the parvovirus B19 VP1u receptor-binding domain. The only known-binder geometry on this epitope.
inputs/1SUV.cif the transferrin complex, fetched to check rather than repeat the brief's claim that this epitope leaves the transferrin site free.
inputs/AF-Q62351-F1.pdb mouse TfR1, an AlphaFold model, residues 123-763. The counter-species target.
inputs/reference-structures/6WRV,6WRW,6WRX.cif further apical-domain references held for calibration.

Every geometric number below was measured by scripts/epitope_analysis.py and is reproducible with one command; it writes notes/epitope-analysis.csv. Deep record: notes/epitope-analysis.md.

what was looked at what was found what it forced
human vs mouse identity 498 of 638 aligned columns = 78.1% confirms the brief, and only visible when the chains are aligned rather than joined on numbering
the species numbering offset mouse minus human is +3 for 359 positions and +2 for 279 — there is an indel never map human to mouse by a fixed offset. A first pass that joined on author numbering reported 5.5% identity against a stated 78% — that impossible number is what exposed the indel
the recommended patch (D204, R208, V210, Y211, N348, K371) five of six substituted in mouse, the sixth falls in the indel; zero conserved; two are below the exposure line, so the usable patch is four residues; max CA-CA span 15.7 Å a binder there is selected for human specificity: objective 3 only
the neighbourhood (every chain-A residue with a heavy atom within 10 Å of a named-patch side chain) 44 residues, 27 conserved in mouse, 10 both conserved and exposed a conserved face sits right beside the recommended one, still inside the apical domain (roughly 189-382)
titratable chemistry at the epitope zero histidines across all 44 residues; 7 Arg/Lys (conserved and exposed: 231 K, 344 K, 374 K); 5 Asp/Glu (conserved and exposed: 343 E, 350 E) the whole switch must be built on the binder; the anchors are 344 K and 374 K, and 343 E / 350 E are positions to keep histidine away from
the N251 glycan NAG linked to N251 by a 1.44 Å bond, 11.2 Å from the named patch and 6.4 Å from the conserved face; the sequon is conserved (human 251-253 → mouse 253-255) drop 231 K from the hotspot sets and screen every footprint for reaching across N251

Two reference points came from outside the structures. The organizers' binder-prescreen carries a TfR1 arm of 6,695 reference sequences (54 confirmed binders, the rest disclosed patent claims), calibrated over 927 fixtures: 103 of 105 verbatim known binders caught, zero target-arm flags on 80 unrelated designs (campaigns/c6-selection/README.md). And the patent record in inputs/poisk-tfr1-records.csv places the brain-shuttle antibody 8D3 at peptides 373-375 — our K374 anchor — and 3M12 at K362-K371, so the chosen anchors sit inside the region real binders use.

Unverified at this level: exposure uses a theoretical maximum-SASA table (Tien et al. 2013) and the deposited coordinates, so it ranks residues and is not absolute; glycan clearance is a distance to the first sugar only.

4. The epitope decision: four patches, one survivor

The measurements produce three candidate sets plus the pair that mattered most (notes/epitope-analysis.md, notes/strategies.md §4):

set residues (11QC chain A) span conserved in mouse glycan clearance serves
E0 named tip 204, 208, 210, 211, 348, 371 15.7 Å 0 of 6 11.2 Å objective 3
E1 north 206, 207, 209, 374 11.8 Å 4 of 4 13.9 Å objectives 1, 2, 3
E2 south 343, 344, 347, 350, 351 14.9 Å 5 of 5 16.2 Å objectives 1, 2, 3
E12 dual anchor 344, 374 — 2 of 2 13.9 Å objectives 1, 2, 3

E1 carries one switch anchor, E2 the other and sits furthest from the glycan, and E12 is just the two anchors — the thinnest possible patch, asking the generator for nothing but the residues the switch needs. Two more sets were tried later: E3 = {231, 344, 374}, a triple-cation set that walks into the glycan, and H = {R208, Y211, K344, K374}, a hybrid of the organizers' tip and our anchors.

Outcome, in one line: E12 advanced; E0 missed by one design; E1 and E2 closed negative; E3 closed as a measured negative; H produced a champion-class design and entered the submission.

The hypothesis the challenge then tested, registered before any generation (notes/strategies.md §3):

A binder on the conserved, glycan-clear face of the apical domain, carrying two or three histidines facing a conserved target lysine, can serve objectives 1 and 2 with the same interface: the epitope is identical in both species, so cross-reactivity follows from the epitope choice, and the switch follows from like-charge repulsion as the histidines protonate near pH 6.

It was made falsifiable at three points, each with a pre-registered discard rule: the conserved face may not dock at all (C1), the histidines may destroy binding (C3), and the linkage sign may come out negative as it did in the TNF-α challenge (C3).

5. The instrument problem: a co-fold screen that cannot read this target

The campaign's defining technical event happened before any design was judged. The standard co-folding screen does not work on TfR1's apical tip, and that was proven with controls rather than guessed.

The fold target was measured first — the plan's one unmeasured risk. A 92-residue binder against the full protomer (Boltz-2, 5 samples, seed 42, receptor MSA capped at 1024 rows, binder on an empty MSA) peaked at 15.61 GiB job RSS and 11.29 GiB of the 12.2 GB card, ~2.5 min for five samples, zero failures. The fold target is the full protomer, numbering fold = author − 121 (notes/c1-triage.md).

The first batch folded and nothing landed. The 96 campaign-1 designs produced 480 models; a v2 screen over 495 samples found not one sample with a binder cleanly on its designed patch in any of the four sets — 69 samples carried an off-site heavy-atom collision and the rest floated. Four controls turned that from a bad day into a finding:

control result what it proves
the TNF-α champion through this exact pipeline and MSA route ipSAE 0.841-0.902 (its own earlier record 0.886) the pipeline is not broken
the native VP1u domain + the 11QC protomer — a binder known to work, from the organizers' own reference complex 0 of 5 samples at the verified footprint, 42-55 Å away, ipSAE 0.000 the model cannot find this epitope even for nature's binder
the same with VP1u's own MSA, and again at 10 samples unchanged, 42-50 Å; 0 of 10 docked not an MSA or sampling artifact
the same against the 221-residue apical block ipTM up to 0.53, but the pose sits on author 303-328, the dimer interface, 33-38 Å away a confident wrong answer, which is worse than none

The native footprint was re-verified straight from 11RN.cif: TfR1 author contacts with VP1u are 202, 203, 204, 208, 209, 210, 211, 212, 348, 371 — identical on both copies (notes/screen-predictor-options.md).

The second folder failed the same way. Chai-1 needed three fixes here (torch 2.14.1+cu130, for sm_120 kernels on an RTX 5070; MSAs converted to .aligned.pqt, since plain .a3m is silently ignored; --no-use-esm-embeddings, after the 5.5 GB ESM download broke twice), then floated the native VP1u 42-55 Å away in all five samples, ipTM 0.19, pTM 0.87, no contacts. The limitation is the target, not a Boltz quirk.

The fix: direct the interface, then only compare. With pocket restraints on the ten footprint residues (8 Å), Chai-1 docks the native domain at the footprint in all five samples — 10-14 of its residues within 5 Å, zero contacts at the dimer patch — and its ipTM rises from 0.19 to 0.42-0.48. The model can build an interface when told where; it cannot find one here. That produced the primary instrument and its permanent caveat:

  • The read: Chai-1 under pocket restraints on the designed anchors, 5 samples, mean ipTM.
  • The calibration: the native known binder reads 0.42-0.48 under the identical protocol; measured dynamic range 0.21-0.75 across designs, replicate spread ±0.02 within a design.
  • The caveat, repeated on every results page: a restrained pose is directed by construction. The number is a consistency read — does this sequence form a coherent interface at the designed site — and not independent evidence of binding.
  • The engagement gate (added 2026-10-27, after it bit): a read counts only when the worst anchor distance is ≤ 8 Å and at least one binder residue sits at the designed site. Without it an off-site pose can read ~0.70 — the E2 design e2_16 read 0.696 while sitting about 55 Å away.

What was demoted rather than dropped. Boltz-2 stayed as a second, diagnostic folder supplying ipSAE and pDockQ2 (Chai-1 writes no PAE, so a second folder is the only route to them); those values are recorded per design and explicitly do not score, stated in the selector's own docstring. pDockQ2 was pre-registered as recorded-not-gated because an earlier calibration found it non-discriminative. A third folder was attempted and failed: OpenFold3 v0.5.1 installed and ran, then died at a triangular-attention layer with CUDA OOM after ~24 minutes on the 715-residue complex, and the allocator workaround crashed the whole WSL host (records/openfold3-attempt-2026-10-30.md). The doctrine in one sentence: every instrument here was first run on something whose answer was already known, and the ones that failed their control became diagnostics rather than being used quietly.

6. The pipeline, stage by stage

The whole pipeline as a funnel: 388 generated backbones across six waves, the filter at every stage, and the tool behind every metric. Green chips are free steps that run on the CPU in seconds, orange chips cost GPU minutes, the pink chip is the verification round only the final twenty earn. The note at the bottom shows the loops that fed new variants back in — the histidine retrofit, the switch-transfer round and the liability repairs all re-entered the funnel as new sequences on proven backbones.

Stage 1 — Generation. Local Genie 3 on one GPU and the hosted NVIDIA RFD4-Proteina NIM, both conditioned on explicit hotspot sets. The generation target is the apical block 180-400 of 11QC chain A (221 contiguous residues, renumbered 1-221, block = author − 179, every hotspot letter asserted after the shift). RFD4 provenance is recorded to the checkpoint (chk_epoch_00000169_step_000000340000-ema.ckpt, NIM 1.0.0, thinking_medium = 60 steps / 185 trunk passes, 8 designs per call, ~2.5 min per call; notes/rfd4-arm.md). Six waves, 388 backbones: 96 + 97 in the triage, 81 in batch 2, 48 in batch 3, 42 in wave 2, 24 two-chain units. Lengths 60-140 aa, mostly 60-110. Generator-side quality across the first RFD4 pool of 97: motif all-atom RMSD ≤ 0.49 Å, clash fraction ≤ 0.0003, sequence adherence 1.0.

Stage 2 — Geometry and glycan screen (free, CPU seconds). scripts/work/screen-gen-geometry.py, pre-registered rule: minimum binder-target CA distance ≥ 3.0 Å, at least 3 target CAs within 8 Å, a designed hotspot within 12 Å. All 96 triage designs passed, each sitting on its designed patch in the generator's own output (hotspot CA-CA 4.3-6.4 Å for E0). The glycan screen is the part that removed designs: 9 of 24 E3 designs and 2 of 24 two-chain units were built into N251 and excluded.

Stage 3 — Sequence assignment. RFD4 designs carry the generator's own sequences; the Genie 3 arm was sequenced with ProteinMPNN on CPU (T = 0.1, seed 37), one sequence per design. An honest divergence: the rule carried forward from the TNF-α challenge was "full-backbone ProteinMPNN, never CA-only" — the same Genie 3 backbone capped at ipSAE 0.248 under CA-only sequencing and produced 18 members at 0.63-0.85 under full-backbone (notes/lessons-c2-c3.md B1) — and campaign 1's own plan repeats it. In execution the Genie 3 arm shipped CA-only sequences in C1 and C2, and eight of the submitted twenty descend from that arm.

Stage 4 — The restrained fold and the engagement gate (GPU minutes). Chai-1, pocket restraints on the designed anchors (8 Å), 5 samples, seed 42, serial on one GPU, ~12 min per design; aggregated by scripts/work/chai-restrained-scores.py, which applies the gate. The advance line was set at 0.45 — level with the native reference's 0.42-0.48. This is the binding instrument for the rest of the challenge, and the only read that scores.

Stage 5 — The switch layer (GPU minutes plus free PROPKA). c3-pick-positions.py selects binder positions whose side chain sits 3.5-8.5 Å from an anchor lysine NZ with relative SASA ≥ 0.20; c3-build-designs.py builds each variant with the parent's own MSA and restraint files, so the only change is the mutated sequence. Mechanism read: PROPKA on the bound and free states of every engineered histidine (c3-histidine-pka.py) plus a Wyman-linkage integration over pH 6.0-7.4 (tools/switch/linkage_score.py). Chapter 7.

Stage 6 — The mouse cross-fold (GPU minutes). c4-prep-mouse-target.py takes the mouse sequence from the AlphaFold model, maps the anchors through the alignment (human K344/K374 → mouse K346/K376 = fold indices 224/254), fetches a depth-1024 MSA, and runs the identical protocol with its own superposition frame. Measures, does not gate. Chapter 8.

Stage 7 — Selection (free, CPU seconds). campaigns/c6-selection/scripts/select-top20.py applies the floors, computes total = 2.0·S + 1.5·X + 1.5·B + 1.0·E, enforces one design per 0.90-identity cluster, and writes the records; build-submission.py writes the upload file from the selector's output with asserts on count and name uniqueness. The final run scored 314 designs, 129 failed the floors, 39 were held as near-neighbours, one was dropped as an identical sequence, and 20 were selected (recomputed from records/selection-all-2026-10-30.csv). Chapter 11.

7. The pH switch: the histidine logic and what was measured

Objective 1, the hardest goal, and the campaign the earlier TNF-α challenge never ran — the direct reason its submission could not claim this objective.

One family, three sequences, one backbone: the campaign-2 parent e12rfd4_r5d1 (restrained 0.779) and its single- and double-histidine switch variants, each folded under the identical restraints against the human apical domain. The engineered histidines face the conserved anchor lysines K344 and K374; nothing else changes between the panels.

Where the histidines went. In the strongest families the picked positions were already carboxylates — the generators had independently aimed an Asp or Glu at the anchor lysines, the same interaction with the opposite sign (notes/c3-switch.md):

family (parent read) site at A223 (author K344) site at A253 (author K374)
e12rfd4_r5d1 (0.779) D27, 4.51 Å, rSASA 0.269 D8, 4.75 Å, rSASA 0.338
e12rfd4_r5d7 (0.761) G43, 4.46 Å, rSASA 0.581 A6, 8.21 Å, rSASA 0.430
e12rfd4_r4d5 (0.710) V28, 6.35 Å, rSASA 0.250 A9, 7.41 Å, rSASA 0.451
e12rfd4_r4d3 (0.682) G16, 8.16 Å, rSASA 0.353 D25, 4.12 Å, rSASA 0.219
e12b2_20 (0.735) K34, 6.42 Å, rSASA 0.353 A15, 3.69 Å, rSASA 0.248

Gate 1 — binding must survive. 29 variants (19 singles, 7 doubles, a three-step ladder), 145 folds; a variant keeps its slot if its mean restrained ipTM is within 0.10 of its parent. 21 of 29 kept. The top family is nearly untouched: parent 0.779 → 0.782 / 0.781 / 0.748 for one, two and three histidines. Eight collapsed; the worst (e12b2_8_s1) lost 0.521, so that position was load-bearing.

The limitation of gate 1, measured rather than argued. The retrofit replaces a deep carboxylate contact with a shallower imidazole one: minimum heavy-atom distance to the anchor NZ is 1.78 Å (D27) and 2.83 Å (D8) in the parent against 3.62 Å (H27) and 3.88 Å (H8) in the variants. The contact is real — the restraints do not invent it — but a flat ipTM on a directed read does not price the loss of a near-covalent salt bridge. Gate 1 selects variants that keep the interface, not necessarily the affinity.

Gate 2 — the linkage sign, and why it was demoted. The registered gate was delta_log_Ka > 0 from the Wyman-linkage scorer (PROPKA pKa bound vs free, integrated over pH 6.0-7.4). 26 of 29 variants move positive against their own parent (sign test p ≈ 1.5e-5). But an external review observed that this is close to the expected output of adding protonatable sites at an interface, and the unmodified parents carry a null with the same scatter: 10 of 81 read positive (~12%), spanning +0.058 to +1.547. The whole b2_20 family's totals (+0.040 / +0.058 / +0.085) land inside the densest part of that null, and the raw top of the entire ranking is an unmodified parent (e12b2_17, +1.547 — the extreme tail of the null, not an artifact: pH-linked behaviour is TfR1's own biology). The gate can still fail, three variants moved negative, but passing it does not demonstrate a switch. It was re-labelled a consistency check (review finding 1, accepted).

The substance — the per-site pKa shift. PROPKA on the bound and the free state of each engineered histidine. The mechanism predicts the bound-state pKa is depressed, because the anchor cation destabilises the protonated form:

variant engineered His pKa shift, bound vs free
c3_e12rfd4_r4d5_d2 (the champion) pos 28 −2.82 — the strongest site in the project
c3_e12b2_20_d2 pos 15 / 34 −2.76 / −2.59
c3_e12b2_20_s2 pos 34 (6.42 Å) −2.16
c3_e12b2_20_s1 pos 15 (3.69 Å) −2.12
c3_e12rfd4_r6d2_s1 pos 52 / 82 −1.47 / 0.00
c3_e12rfd4_r5d1_s1 pos 27 (4.51 Å) −1.35
c3_e12rfd4_r5d1_s2 pos 8 (4.75 Å) −0.63 → unresolved
c3_e12rfd4_r5d1_l3 pos 31 (free pKa 7.09) −0.53 → unresolved
c3_e12b2_26_s2 (control, 8.05 Å, far edge) pos 20 −0.05, flat
c3_e12rfd4_r6d5_s2 (control, 8.42 Å, far edge) pos 25 −0.15, flat
c3_e12rfd4_r4d3_d2 (control) pos 25 +0.48, wrong direction

The controls are the point: positions at the far edge of the engage window shift by −0.05 and −0.15 and their variants' totals go negative, and the one wrong-direction site drags its variant's total negative too. The instrument separates engaging from non-engaging sites at the strong end only — PROPKA's error on experimental benchmarks is about 0.8 pH units, larger than the 0.4-0.5 gap at the weak end, so the −0.53 and −0.63 sites are recorded as unresolved, not engaging (reviewer finding 2, 2026-10-27).

The ladder. On the top family the totals increase strictly with histidine count and separate by count with no overlap: 0 (the parent) −0.057; one +0.029, +0.076, +0.146; two +0.560, +0.625; three +0.708. Under the re-framed gate 2 that dose-response is consistency rather than independent evidence — but it is the shape a working dose series has, and it ships as the declared mechanism control the organizers' rules allow. (A correction is on the record: an earlier note called the ladder "not monotone"; that sentence was wrong, and the reason to withhold magnitudes is the null scatter, not non-monotonicity.)

Tuning guidance for the next batch. The free pKas cluster at 5.92-6.37 with one at 7.09. A histidine at free pKa 6.0 is roughly 4% protonated at pH 7.4 and 50% at 6.0 — a working but shallow switch. The 7.4 → 6.0 window is exercised hardest by free pKas near 6.8-7.0, so the designed positions should aim there; the best-placed site measured (r5d1_l3 pos 31, free pKa 7.09) also shows the smallest bound shift, so position choice and pull can work against each other.

A design-side arm. Proton-PottsMPNN redesigns an interface with explicit protonation-state tokens. It was run off-label for this direction — the engine's own campaigns pin the protonated state, while we pinned the neutral HIS-S so the bound complex favours it and acidification releases. The first sweep degenerated at high selectivity weight into His/Arg-rich near-homopolymers; a capped rerun (≤ 12 mutations) gave four sane variants, best ppmpnn_r4d5_l01_s0 at 0.752 engaged, 0.008 below its parent while carrying the designed switch. The arm closed at parity: it showed the switch can be designed in rather than screened for, and it did not beat the retrofit.

8. The mouse axis: measuring the species gap

The champion c3_e12rfd4_r4d5_d2 folded under the identical restrained protocol against the human apical domain (restrained ipTM 0.782, 5 of 5 samples engaged) and against the mouse receptor (0.688). Only the target changes: the same sequence, the same restraint set mapped through the alignment to mouse K346/K376, the same five samples.

Campaign 4 generates nothing and modifies nothing, which is what makes the species difference readable (notes/c4-mouse.md, campaigns/c4-mouse-crossfold/mouse-scores.csv). The bands were fixed before the run: within 0.05 of the human read = top, within 0.15 = second, clearly weaker = third, human-only = floor.

c3_e12rfd4_r3d4_d2 0.603 0.621 +0.018 top
e12b2_31 0.507 0.453 −0.053 top
e12b2_29 0.615 0.550 −0.065 second
c3_e12rfd4_r4d5_d2 0.688 0.782 +0.094 second
e12rfd4_r6d2 0.633 0.738 +0.105 second
c3_e12rfd4_r5d7_d2 0.579 0.777 +0.198 third

  1. The tightest human designs are the weakest cross-reads. The three strongest human parents fall from 0.779 / 0.761 / 0.735 to 0.364 / 0.266 / 0.257, deltas +0.42 to +0.50. Human affinity and species transfer are opposed in this data — the inverse of the TNF-α lesson, where cross-reactivity came only from tight designs.
  2. Two designs are mouse-competent, and one carries the switch. e12rfd4_r4d5 (mouse 0.760, delta −0.050) and c3_e12rfd4_r3d4_d2 (0.603, +0.018, top band and a switch variant with site shifts −0.39 and −2.13). The best mouse read in the project belongs to a sibling, c3_e12rfd4_r4d5_s2 at 0.768.
  3. The histidine retrofits improve the mouse read in most families — r5d7 0.266 → 0.579, r5d1 0.364 → 0.545/0.551, r3d4 0.528 → 0.603, while r4d5 stays strong and b2_20 is unchanged near 0.26. Recorded as an observation, with no explanation claimed.

Coverage grew with the campaign: 33 designs and 165 samples at first (20 from C2 plus 13 from C3), then 58, then 63 designs including every member of the final twenty, which is what the selector's mouse component ranks on.

The caveat, restated in the campaign's own record. A co-folding model scoring two receptors it was never trained to discriminate is weak evidence about species selectivity; two designs can score identically and behave differently in the lab; the mouse structure is a prediction and the human one experimental. The claim supported is "the epitope is conserved and the interface reads on both receptors" — not "the KD ratio is near 1".

9. The campaigns, one by one

Six campaigns. Not every one is the same kind of experiment: C1 is the only one whose deliverable is a decision rather than designs; C2 varies the generator; C3 the chemistry; C4 the species, and generates nothing; C5 the architecture; C6 adds no designs at all and re-reads, ranks and repairs.

C1 — the epitope triage (2026-10-23 → 10-25, re-screen 10-27)

Tools: Genie 3, ProteinMPNN, RFD4-Proteina NIM, Boltz-2, IPSAE, Chai-1 with pocket restraints, the 11RN native complex as control. Strategy: generate against four apical patches with two independent generators, then decide by a pre-registered rule on a screen validated with controls.

The per-design cost of the campaign-1 pipeline — the two folds dominate at about 80% of the wall time. The companion diagram viewers/c1-strategy-comparison.png contrasts the local Genie 3 path with the hosted RFD4 path.

Numbers: 96 Genie 3 designs (24 per set) and 97 hosted RFD4 designs, all passing the geometry screen; 480 fold models and a v2 screen over 495 samples returning zero clean at-site samples (chapter 5); then the directed re-read of 48 designs, 240 samples, under the amended rule (a set advances when ≥ 25%, i.e. ≥ 6 of 24, reach mean restrained ipTM ≥ 0.45):

set n ≥ 0.45 ≥ 0.50 median top three
E0 24 5 (21%) 4 0.388 e0_22 0.556, e0_21 0.543, e0_19 0.520
E12 24 8 (33%) 7 0.324 e12_18 0.752, e12_9 0.655, e12_6 0.639

Verdict: E12 advances; E0 is one design short and is carried as a secondary arm, not eliminated. The margin is reported for what it is: E0's median is higher (0.388 vs 0.324) and E12's win rides its upper tail; Fisher's exact on 5/24 vs 8/24 is p = 0.52, so the sets are statistically indistinguishable on the deciding metric; and counting designs with any sample ≥ 0.45 would give E0 exactly 6 of 24 and advance it. A second-seed rerun of the four near-line designs settled the count rather than the significance — pooled means 0.433, 0.441, 0.430, 0.436, all under 0.45, so E0 stands at 5 of 24 on both seeds.

Two guards ran before the verdict was signed. The restraint-count confound: the sets carry different numbers of hotspots (E0 six, E2 five, E1 four, E12 two), so two E0 designs were re-scored with only two restraints — 0.412 and 0.405 against 0.400 and 0.437 at six, no jump toward the E12 range (0.655, 0.752), so the confound is falsified. And the v1 screen correction: v1's clash test looked only at the designed residues, and under v2's minimum-over-all-atoms test all 12 samples v1 had called clean carry an off-site collision of 1.6-2.6 Å.

The deferred screen, and its outcome. E1 and E2 were left unscreened by explicit decision on 2026-10-25 — at p = 0.52 between the measured sets, nine GPU-hours would buy completeness prose, not a decision. The screen ran anyway on 10-27 as the fallback task during an RFD4 outage: all 48 C1-era E1/E2 designs folded, 0 of 48 engaged their designed site (E1: 2 of 24 above the bar, best e1_13 0.491, no binder residue within 5 Å of any anchor, worst-anchor 26-59 Å; E2: 5 of 24, best e2_16 0.696 with its pose at author 629-760, ~55 Å away). Both sets closed negative, and that is where the engagement gate came from.

C2 — the binding families and their generator arms (2026-10-25 → 10-28)

Tools: Genie 3, RFD4-Proteina NIM, ProteinMPNN, Chai-1 with pocket restraints. Strategy: turn the surviving epitope into a family, with two generators and no pre-selection — geometry screen only, then fold everything.

Numbers: 32 Genie 3 + 49 RFD4 = 81 designs, 405 folds; 20 cleared the 0.45 line, 17 at ≥ 0.50, 13 at ≥ 0.60, top e12rfd4_r5d1 at 0.779. The pool is materially stronger than campaign 1's (17 vs 7 at 0.50; top 0.779 vs 0.752), all above the native reference ceiling of 0.48. Generator comparison: RFD4 11 of 49 (22%), Genie 3 9 of 32 (28%), Fisher p = 0.605 — statistically indistinguishable. The TNF-α lesson that the generator dominates the outcome motivated running both arms; this screen cannot separate them, and that is recorded rather than spun.

Robustness incident. A host display-driver crash (nvlddmkm 0xD1) killed the pass at 44 of 81. It resumed on driver 621.01 with PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:False, a WSL GPU-PV allocator workaround that touches memory handling only. The design killed mid-fold (e12rfd4_r4d3) completed on resume at 0.682, and the pre- and post-crash halves are consistent. Wall span 16 hours, ~11.5 of them folding.

Batch 3 (10-26/27): 39 designs, 195 samples, zero fold failures. The E12 extension added 24 designs, 4 at the bar (17%, the same band as the arm's own 22%), and produced a co-champion — b3_E12_r90003 at 0.776, a statistical tie with r5d1 — plus b3_E12_r110007 at 0.692. The E3 triple-cation set closed as a measured negative on three agreeing reads: 1 of 15 at the bar against the rule's 4, hotspot obedience 0.50, 9 of 24 generated designs built into the N251 glycan and excluded, and the folded remainder below the E12 class (median 0.274 vs 0.292, top 0.472).

Wave 2 (10-27/28): the RFD4 arm folded 26 of 26 and an RFdiffusion arm 16 of 16, zero failures. The long-length extension (110-140 aa) did not beat the short champions (best engaged 0.420) and 22 designs above 126 aa stay held as the host-crash class. But the hybrid set H = {R208, Y211, K344, K374} delivered b4_H_r1d0000 at 0.777 (5 of 5 engaged, champion class) and b4_H_r1d0004 at 0.645; their switch variants are in the submitted twenty.

C3 — the pH switch layer (2026-10-26, transfer round 10-29)

Tools: the vendored switch geometry and rSASA filter, Chai-1 with pocket restraints, PROPKA, the Wyman-linkage scorer, Proton-PottsMPNN. Strategy: change the designs' chemistry, not their origin or target, and re-read every variant with the identical instrument so it compares directly to its parent. Chapter 7 is the full account: 29 variants, 145 folds, 21 keeping their binding, per-site shifts −0.5 to −2.8 at engaging sites and flat at the far window edge, 13 carrying forward. The switch-transfer round (10-29) then built ten histidine variants on the three strongest-binding switch-less parents; the winner c3_b4_H_r1d0000_53h keeps its parent's binding (restrained 0.768, unrestrained 0.771 at 5 of 5) and replaced it in the twenty. Its sibling 49h carries the project's strongest linkage total (+1.153, a modelled 14.2× selectivity) and heads the reserve — recorded, and deliberately not quoted as a prediction.

C4 — the mouse cross-fold (2026-10-26, extended 10-28/29)

Tools: Chai-1 with pocket restraints, ColabFold MSAs (depth 1024), alignment-derived anchors. 33 designs and 165 samples at first, 63 by the end; two mouse-competent candidates. Chapter 8.

C5 — two-chain units against the single-chain class (10-26 → 10-29)

Tools: RFD4-Proteina (two designed segments), ProteinMPNN, Chai-1, Boltz-2, IPSAE, DockQ, PRODIGY. Strategy: the only campaign with a second designed chain — a pair that must hold the target and each other — asking whether that beats the single-chain class at E12.

Generation worked immediately: the hosted request was extended with a second expandable segment (chain C, entity 2, its own length range) and the endpoint accepted it with zero validation errors, 8 designs in 95 seconds. Of 24 designs, 23 form a real B-C unit covering both anchor lysines, 2 were excluded by the glycan screen, 22 went to folding.

The registered test could not run on this host: the assembled three-chain fold sits at 11.9 of 12.2 GB VRAM and runs its trunk about 10× slow (775 s per recycle against an 82 s baseline). Two attempts, one from a cold boot; the first ended in a host crash. The read was taken per chain instead — 44 folds, all complete — and on the honest aggregation (the minimum of the two chains, since both must bind) the best unit reads 0.356; on the mean the best is 0.502 (c5_r3d6, whose B chain reads 0.702 and C chain 0.303 — exactly the case a mean flatters); zero designs reach 0.70 either way, and DockQ against the design models is 0.00-0.19 for almost all. But a chain designed to brace against both the target and its partner, folded without its partner, should read low, so both numbers are the expected result of the adaptation and are recorded as inconclusive, not negative. A reviewer made the same point formally: the registered discard rule fired on profile conditions (B-C intact, clashes) that were only ever measurable on the assembled fold. A numbering incident was caught before the verdict was signed — nine fallback restraint files carried author instead of sequence numbering (off by 121), so those folds were conditioned 39-48 Å from their intended residues; after the fix every corrected fold sits 3.4-9.5 Å from its restraining residue, reads moved by −0.17 to +0.13, and two designs that the mis-conditioning had flattered dropped to the floor class.

The rescue, which did run (10-28/29): all 22 assembled units folded against the 221-residue apical block — the cheap target that fits — with Boltz-2, pocket restraints on both binders at the E12 anchors (block numbering 165/195), 5 samples each. Recomputed from records/c5-rescue-block-2026-10-29.csv: 110 samples, 74 engage both binders at the anchors, 19 of 22 designs have at least one such sample, 9 of 22 engage in all five, the designed B-C brace forms (contacts 1.8-2.9 Å), and the best units read mean ipTM 0.958 (r1d0001; best single model 0.9616), 0.923 and 0.901.

Verdict: the assembled units assemble; only the full-protomer assembled fold remains out of reach here. The direction is recorded as a capability, not a competitor — the rescue used a different target and restraint set, and no comparable read exists against the single-chain class, which carries the submission (all twenty entries declared single_chain). Two instruments were calibrated inside this campaign and then used elsewhere: DockQ v2, verified by scoring an existing design's fold against its own design model at 0.897 total, iRMSD 0.55 Å (measured on e12rfd4_r4d5, the champion's parent), and PRODIGY, which reproduced the published affinity estimate on the native 11RN interface (1.3-1.7 µM against about 1 µM published) before being pointed at any design (campaigns/c5-multi-chain/research.md).

C6 — evaluation, refinement and the final twenty (10-27 → 10-30)

Tools: the selector, binder-prescreen v0.5, MMseqs2, US-align, Foldseek, Chai-1, Boltz-2, IPSAE, PROPKA 3.5.1, Mol. Strategy: add no designs; re-read what C2-C4 produced, rank it, and repair the survivors' weaknesses. The count grew across three runs — 245 scored on the first pass (98 failing the floors), 293 on the completed pool, 314 on the final run with the switch-transfer variants and the liability repairs added. Membership of the twenty survived the from-scratch re-run with two adjacent ranks swapped: robustness evidence gathered after* the selection was frozen, where it could only have embarrassed the result (notes/review-2026-10-30.md).

Four verification rounds landed inside this campaign.

  1. The multi-tool confidence matrix (10-28). Boltz-2 restrained folds plus ipSAE cover the whole top-32 pool, every pose on-site under the engagement gate, later filled to all twenty. b3_E12_r90003 is the most cross-validated design in the project (Chai 0.776, Boltz ipTM 0.808, ipSAE 0.50, pDockQ2 0.43) and sits at rank 15 because its switch evidence is thin, while the r4d5 and r5d1 champions carry the top Chai reads with low ipSAE. No single in-silico metric decides.
  2. The unrestrained read — the honest test (10-29). Every final design re-folded with no restraints, 5 samples. 11 of 20 find the designed site on their own; 5 in every sample — 53h 0.771, the champion 0.725, e12_9 0.688, r5d1_d2 0.681, 21h 0.667. The other nine read high only under restraints and are restraint-dependent, recorded openly (records/unrestrained-engagement-2026-10-29.csv).
  3. Novelty (10-28). Prescreen v0.5, TfR1 arm, 6,695 references: 20 of 20 pass with no prior-art or known-binder flags. Structural arm (US-align, coverage-aware) against the three known-binder reference structures held here: 0 of 20 hit TM > 0.5 across more than 70% of the design; the maximum is 0.49 (53h vs VP1u) at 47% coverage, so even the near-miss is not one. Within the batch, median pairwise TM 0.37-0.38 and 8 fold clusters.
  4. The liability repair round (10-30). Chapter 12.

11. How the designs were evaluated, and how "better" was decided

The bars were pre-registered on 2026-10-23, before any generation (notes/strategies.md §7), and the selector is the single writer of the ranking (campaigns/c6-selection/scripts/select-top20.py).

Step 1 — the floors, in code and not in prose. pLDDT ≥ 63; sequence entropy ≥ 2.5 bits; no residue above 45% of the chain; no homopolymer run of 6 or more; at least one engaged fold sample. They exist because the previous challenge's floors were promised in prose and applied by no code, which let a 24-residue design that was 64% alanine rank 20th. On the final run 129 of 314 designs failed them, 66 for having no engaged fold sample at all.

Step 2 — the composite. total = 2.0·S + 1.5·X + 1.5·B + 1.0·E, maximum 30, normalised to 100:

term weight what it measures bands
S switch 2.0 the hardest goal 5 for ≥ 2 sites with binding retention ≥ 0.85; 4 for ≥ 2 sites, or 1 site at retention ≥ 0.90; 3 for one site; 2 if the linkage moves the wrong way whatever the count; 1 for a parent with no switch layer
X mouse 1.5 objective 2 5 at ≥ 0.70, 4 at ≥ 0.60, 3 at ≥ 0.50, 2 at ≥ 0.40, 1 otherwise or with no engaged mouse read
B binding 1.5 objective 3, engagement-gated 5 at ≥ 0.70, 4 at ≥ 0.60, 3 at ≥ 0.50, 2 at ≥ 0.45, 1 below
E expression 1.0 the risk of never making it mean of a pLDDT band and a Kyte-Doolittle hydropathy band

S carries the heaviest weight because the organizers' own prompt says a weak but clearly pH-sensitive binder beats a strong insensitive one, and X rides above B because the challenge ranks mouse second and affinity third.

Step 3 — the direction gate. A linkage total moving the wrong way caps S at 2 however many sites a design carries. Added with the switch-transfer round, it immediately moved two high-ipTM designs (r6d2_s1, b2_26_s1) out of the S5 class.

Step 4 — diversity on the provable axis. At most one design per 0.90-identity cluster, stricter than the prescreen's 0.95 within-batch rule; near-neighbours become the ranked reserve. On the final run 39 designs were held this way and one as an identical sequence. The rationale is the novelty rule's own shape: novelty is judged per structural backbone, so twenty sequences on two backbones carry two identities and one fold resembling something known removes every design built on it. The twenty sit on twenty distinct backbones. Ties break on switch evidence, then binding, then the least-represented family.

Step 5 — the pre-flight assertions. Every design has a row in every screen; every design has a human fold and a mouse fold, or it scores the X floor and the record says why; every switch claim has a linkage row; every design has an at-site contact; and the sequence in the CSV is compared to the sequence that was folded by hash, not by name. Each exists because its absence caused a real error in an earlier challenge.

What "better" explicitly did not mean. Not the highest single read: the top Chai ipTM in the pool (0.802, c3_e12b2_20_s2) is not rank 1, and the most cross-validated design is rank 15. Not ipSAE: recorded for all twenty, scoring nothing, because Boltz-2 fails its control here. Not the linkage magnitude: the strongest linkage in the project sits in the reserve. Rank 1 is the one design that carries all three objectives at once.

The underlying screen (records/developability-qc-2026-10-29.csv) found zero N-glycosylation sequons in the shipped sequences — the one that matters most for cell-free expression — 11 designs carrying a deamidation motif (mostly the moderate DS/DG class), one with an odd free cysteine, and 9 of 20 carrying a flagged position at or next to the binding interface, where deamidation could erode binding over time. That last number is itself a correction: an earlier record claimed the flagged motifs sat outside the interface, and checking each against its fold's contact map showed seven of them do not.

13. What is honest and what is not yet known

  • Nothing here is wet-lab validated. No record in this challenge reports an experimental measurement of any design. The few affinity figures that appear (PRODIGY's 1.3-1.7 µM on the native interface, the published ~1 µM it was calibrated against, the TNF-α campaign's outcomes) belong to other molecules.
  • The primary instrument is a directed read. The restrained co-fold builds the interface it then scores. The native known binder calibrates at 0.42-0.48 and our champions sit near 0.78, clearly above it and reproducibly so (±0.02 within a design, top three within 0.09 on a second seed) — but a consistency read is not independent evidence of binding. Only 11 of the 20 find their site with no restraints, and the other nine are recorded as restraint-dependent.
  • Against the one wet-lab-calibrated metric available, the file reads weak. In the released TNF-α campaign, designs in the ipSAE 0.6-0.7 band bound 0 of 22 while the ≥ 0.8 band bound 25.7% against a base rate of 8.7%. Our twenty have median ipSAE 0.014 and 19 of 20 below 0.6. The mitigating facts are that Boltz-2 — the folder ipSAE comes from — fails its own control on this target, and that in the same calibration one real binder at 2.1 nM scored 0.06. Neither makes the number good.
  • The switch is a direction, not a magnitude. The registered sign gate was demoted once the parent null was measured (10 of 81 unmodified parents read positive, +0.058 to +1.547). The substantive evidence is the per-site pKa depression, and PROPKA's own error is about 0.8 units, so only shifts beyond about 1 unit discriminate. Four of the project's S5 designs carry such a site; the rest rest on site count and direction alone.
  • Two of the five S5 designs carry one engineered histidine, not two. The S5 band reads "two or more sites", and the selector takes that count from the linkage scorer's effective_sites column where one exists, overriding the engineered-histidine count in campaigns/c3-switch-layer/variants.csv. For 53h and b2_20_s2_n10q that means one designed histidine counted as two effective titratable sites, while the previous README, notes/self-evaluation.md and the campaign README describe both as "two engineered sites".
  • The mouse comparison is experimental structure against predicted structure, and a co-folding model asked to discriminate two receptors it was never trained to discriminate is weak evidence about species selectivity.
  • The glycan is one sugar. Every glycan clearance here is a distance to the first NAG; a real N-glycan extends 10-20 Å further and no model in this stack represents it. The E3 verdict is based on distance, not steric calculation.
  • The dimer was answered geometrically, not folded. All folds are single-protomer by host necessity; the full 1,278-residue dimer is out of reach on a 12 GB card and was never attempted. The avidity the dimer allows — a target in solution binding two immobilised designs at once — can flatter the sensorgram and complicate the KD fit, and nothing here models it.
  • The multi-chain direction is a capability read, not a comparison. The rescue proves the two-chain units assemble; it does not show them better or worse than the single-chain class.
  • A stated rule was not followed. "Full-backbone ProteinMPNN, never CA-only" was carried forward as a hard lesson and written into campaign 1's plan; the Genie 3 arm shipped CA-only sequences in C1 and C2, and eight of the submitted twenty descend from it.
  • Several records lag the set they describe. The 2026-10-29 verification records (unrestrained engagement, developability, structural novelty) describe the two liability repairs' parents, because the repairs entered the file on 10-30. The missing reads exist — in liability-round-2026-10-30.csv, structural-novelty-2026-10-30.csv and the mouse record — so the "20 of 20" coverage claims hold only when two records are read together. A review caught this as the third occurrence of the same pattern, and the fix was structural: the selector now regenerates its coverage record as its last step.

14. Where the records disagree

designs scored the previous README says 336; methodology.md and design-method.md say 293; the live record holds 314 records/selection-scores-2026-10-30.csv = 314. The 336 is the master inventory's count of designed chains; 293 is the previous run
master inventory notes/best-designs-by-campaign-2026-10-30.md says 470 entries and "327 unique designed-binder sequences, 372 unique sequences"; an earlier commit message says 417 / 400 the file: 470 rows (336 designs, 72 two-chain unit chains, 62 mouse-crossfold entries), 372 unique sequences

best two-chain unit c5.../results.md and the best-designs note say 0.962; the previous README and lineage.json say 0.958 both, under different definitions: r1d0001's best single model is 0.9616 and its mean over five models 0.958. e12rfd4_r4d5's human read notes/campaign-summary-2026-10-28.md lists 0.760, the same value as its mouse read 0.710, per c2.../results.md and notes/c4-mouse.md; the summary appears to have copied the mouse column
closest prescreen similarity notes/self-evaluation.md and lineage.json say "≤ 0.28" the report: whole-sequence identity against all 6,695 references is 0.0, while the region arm reaches 0.32 (records/prescreen-report-2026-10-30.csv); both 0.32 hits are disclosed patent claims, which the tool does not let decide a verdict
pLDDT and hydropathy of the twenty notes/self-evaluation.md says "pLDDT 78-90" and hydropathy "in the +0.05 to +0.30 band" the record: pLDDT 71.3-89.7 (e12b2_29 is 71.3) and hydropathy −1.42 to +1.23
per-site pKa of the switch-transfer winners the previous README, the notes and the campaign README quote −2.14 for 53h not in the primary record: campaigns/c3-switch-layer/pka-per-site.txt was last extended 2026-10-28, before the transfer round, and holds no row for 53h or 13_48; its "S5 addendum" also still describes "the six S5 designs in the final twenty", two of which the direction gate later demoted. The −2.14 is sourced only to prose
the arrows in pka-per-site.txt the header says "delta = bound − free" and the main table reads free → bound (6.35 → 5.41, −0.94), while the S5 addendum reads the other way (3.41 → 6.23, −2.82) the deltas are consistent and negative throughout; the addendum's arrows are reversed relative to the header
DockQ 0.897 "on the champion" methodology.md and design-method.md attribute it to the champion c5.../research.md records it on e12rfd4_r4d5 — the champion's parent
b3_E12_r90003's rank notes/self-evaluation.md places it at rank 13 the submission file and the selection record put it 15th
the switch column in records/coverage-2026-10-30.csv reads no for all twenty, including the five S5 designs a defect in the selector's coverage writer: it reads a key named ph that the score row never sets (select-top20.py, ~line 505). Harmless to the ranking, misleading in the record
ipSAE definition the selector records the maximum over five Boltz-2 models; records/ipsae-pool-2026-10-28.csv records the mean both are labelled in their own files, and for most designs they are close (the champion reads 0.012 either way), but they are not the same quantity
within-batch fold diversity lineage.json reports median pairwise TM 0.37 with "one pair at 0.99"; the self-evaluation reports median 0.38, max 0.57, "no near-identical fold pair at all" both describe real states at different times: the 0.99 pair (the champion and its Proton-PottsMPNN sibling) was moved to the reserve after review

Folder structure

challenges/04-tfr1/
├── README.md        this document
├── lineage.json     the campaign record the local web app renders
├── docs/figures/    the figures embedded above, plus a self-contained HTML build
├── campaigns/       one directory per campaign: its scripts, specs and results
├── records/         every measured table - selection, engagement, novelty, prescreen
├── notes/           the dated working log, the brief, the strategies and the lessons
├── submission/      the uploaded CSV, the methodology and the design-method text
├── scripts/work/    the scripts that produced the screens and the scores
├── nim/             target files prepared for the hosted RFdiffusion4 NIM
├── inputs/          committed target files (11QC, the mouse model)
├── viewers/         Mol* multiview pages and the pipeline diagrams
├── runs/            run outputs, gitignored - `pdt exp status`
└── submission-package-2026-10-30.zip   the package as uploaded

The fold outputs live outside the repo under ~/c4-work/.
